title: Removing Minimum Number of Magic Beans
summary: Given an array of positive integers representing the number of magic beans in each bag, remove the minimum number of beans such that all non-empty bags contain an equal number of beans.
statement: Given an array of positive integers representing the number of magic beans in each bag, remove the minimum number of beans such that all non-empty bags contain an equal number of beans. Once a bean is removed from a bag, it cannot be returned to any other bag.
constraints: Each bag starts with a positive bean count.
After removals, every nonempty bag must contain the same target count; bags may be emptied.
Return the minimum total number of removed beans.
hints: An optimal positive target equals the original count of some surviving bag.
Sort counts; for target beans[i], empty earlier bags and trim all later bags to that target.
Compute total - value*(n-index) for every sorted index and take the minimum.
Between existing counts, increasing the target only reduces removals until reaching the next count, so an optimum occurs at a listed value.
editorial: Between existing counts, increasing the target only reduces removals until reaching the next count, so an optimum occurs at a listed value.

tests.explanation: Keeping target four empties the one-bean bag and trims six and five, removing 4 beans total.
Keeping target two removes six from the ten-bean bag and one from the three-bean bag, totaling 7.
